evidence: The implicit default: unk1B is get_random_nonzero() % 4, so 0-3, and cases 0-3 are all named.
On stage 0 the last tile starts the boss music: func_8001653C (PSX/PC) drives the CD audio player, saturn_music_play the Saturn sound driver.

Leaving a zone whose bit is set calls stop_sound (SsUtSetVVol/SsUtKeyOffV on the zone's SPU voices) before clearing the bit; the tests cannot observe the SPU key-off, so they do not leave a sounding zone.
The substage-0 test only decides whether stop_sound keys off the zone's SPU voices.
Both halves of active != 3 \&\& active != 6 (two overlapping substage-1 zones keep their shared sound) only decide whether stop_sound keys off SPU voices.
No palette animator script list (palette_animator_scripts_* in stage_object_records.c) holds a NULL entry, and the stages without animators have a NULL list that the lookup would index first.
In the clear-all path (unk2 == -1) the object itself has unk2 -1, so current != self is only ever evaluated (and true) for other filters with unk2 == 2.
The implicit default of switch (unk5): unk5 is only ever set to 0-3 (the init, this function's own steps), all named.
Step 1 starts the stage music's CD load (func_80013AD8 polls CdReady and queues CdRead on the PSX/PC); the Saturn build uses its own archive-queue load instead.
After a belt push the scanner is always in state 1 (every belt case sets arg0->state = 1 before the push), so a push onto tile 0 never finds state 2 here.
ABS's first side (unk18.i.hi < x_pos.i.hi) inside the branch for x_pos.val < unk18.val: a smaller fixed-point x cannot have a larger integer part.
ABS's first side (x_pos.i.hi < unk18.i.hi) inside the branch for x_pos.val > unk18.val: a larger fixed-point x cannot have a smaller integer part.
inside is only ever set to 1 (line 61) or left at 0, which returns at line 62, so inside != 1 never holds when the timer is reloaded (the 0x8C reload and the groups' second column are never used).
Saturn machine branch (no llvm-cov branch): the sign fix-up SH-GCC emits for a signed %; get_random_nonzero() returns 1..255, so the dividend is never negative.
